caption.old: E-arm proxy-reward calibration. Points: bin means; bars: 95\% CIs.
caption.new: E-arm proxy-reward reliability (bin means; 95\% CIs).
accepted: E-arm proxy-reward calibration. Points: bin means; bars: 95\% CIs.

Descriptive reliability of the E-archive logged reward, shown separately by target. Pre-update probabilities are grouped into ten fixed equal-width bins; dots show the mean prediction and episode-weighted reward frequency. The dashed diagonal denotes perfect calibration. Whiskers are percentile 95\% CIs from 2,000 resamples of whole runs within target; bins represented by fewer than two runs have no CI. Lower strips give exact episode counts; empty bins have no estimate. Only records with positive mutation counts are included. The reward marks native coverage-save events, which may include hit-count novelty; it is not independently replayed source-branch gain. Episodes have unequal energy and no verified completion flag. Nominal $N=10$; actual $n$ and episode count $m$ are shown.

caption.old: Branch endpoints (top) and AUCs (bottom), mean $\pm$ SD.
caption.new: Branch endpoints (top) and AUCs (bottom), mean $\pm$ SD.

Archive-derived final code-branch count / branch-coverage AUC (branch-hours). Each cell shows mean $\pm$ sample SD and observed $n$ on the first line, with AUC on the second line. The nominal target is 10 runs; all 45 main target--arm groups have observations. Missing runs are not imputed. These descriptive endpoints do not replace matched-horizon causal inference.

caption.old: A--E code-branch trajectories: medians and interquartile ranges.
caption.new: A--E code-branch trajectories (median and interquartile range).
accepted: A--E code-branch trajectories: medians and interquartile ranges.

Observed A--E code-branch trajectories from 465 archives. Time is measured from each fuzzer\_stats start time. Lines are medians and shaded regions are interquartile ranges, computed on a five-minute grid by linear interpolation only between recorded observations. A run contributes neither before its first observation nor after its last; the actual contributing $n$ at 24 hours is shown in A--E order. The plot displays 0--24 hours without imposing a completed 24-hour campaign on interrupted runs. Full time-dependent denominators accompany the figure data; the nominal target remains $N=10$. All 45 main target--arm combinations are represented, including ten E--bftpd archives. Native pipeline/build comparability remains unverified; these curves are descriptive, and shaded ranges are not CIs.

caption.old: E-arm state histories: pre-update probabilities (top) and scheduling multipliers (bottom).
caption.new: E-arm pre-update probabilities (top) and scheduling multipliers (bottom).
accepted: E-arm state histories: pre-update probabilities (top) and scheduling multipliers (bottom).

State-level E-archive illustrations for the three motivating targets, selected by the deterministic rule in the text. Upper panels show pre-update probabilities; lower panels show the logged final selection score divided by the frontier score. Each point is positioned at the logged episode-end time; connecting lines only guide the eye. Zero-frontier records have an undefined multiplier and are omitted from the lower panels. Colors identify states within each target, not equivalent states across targets. Unequal mutation energy, possible posterior resets, and native save-event rewards limit interpretation. The selected source paths and exact plotted values accompany the figure.

On the vulnerable image, 172 of the 233 in-campaign inputs trigger the ASan heap-buffer-overflow predicate in \texttt{make\_ftp\_cmd}; all 172 carry that frame and no other signature appears. The patched image shows no ASan activation for any of the 242 inputs. The 61 non-reproducing inputs and the 9 teardown inputs may require campaign state that a standalone replay does not reconstruct; the in-campaign forensic sidecars recorded almost no usable ASan output, so the pair replay is the authoritative verdict. Second, all 88 LIVE555 campaign crash inputs were replayed against the campaign build, which contains no sanitizer: 82 terminate the server and 6 do not. This establishes reproduction on that build only; without a patched counterpart or sanitizer output it does not attribute the crashes to the use-after-free. Third, all 253 Kamailio queue entries carrying an oversized Content-Length were replayed on the \texttt{o-kam-01} pair: 102 produce the negative-value overflow artifact on the vulnerable build and none on the patched build. All three replays are artifact-level measurements: they provide no arm-level recall, time-to-trigger, or cost denominators.
